rules.rule: end the post on the last concrete beat and cut the final one or two lines when they restate the lesson, give a moral, or add a sign-off like 'that is all'.
rules.evidence: 9 pairs (1, 5, 6, 10, 11, 13, 15, 17, 37). e.g. draft ended 'the details are not decoration / they are the whole argument' and published ended on 'subtly tells people the opposite'.

rules.rule: when a draft stacks three or more parallel 'not x' or 'no x' lines, keep only the one or two that carry the point and cut the rest.
rules.evidence: 5 pairs (12, 16, 28, 29, 39). e.g. 'not the words / not the offers / not the testimonials / the FEELING' became 'not the words / not the offers / the FEELING'.

rules.rule: state general truths and claims about how things work in the present tense, not the past.
rules.evidence: 4 pairs (1, 2, 3, 4). e.g. 'your visitors only ever saw one / so yours had to be the one that won' became 'only ever see one / so yours has to be the one that won'.

rules.rule: when a line ends with a 'not x' contrast or joins two clauses with no break, put the contrast or second clause on its own line.
rules.evidence: 4 pairs (16, 19, 20, 21). e.g. 'the website was INVISIBLE not broken' became 'the website was INVISIBLE' / 'not broken'.

rules.rule: where the draft makes a point and moves on, add a short casual or deadpan aside of one line. it can be a joke, a blunt kicker, or a flat clarification. don't add a polished moral.
rules.evidence: 6 pairs (4, 19, 34, 35, 40, 42). e.g. added 'that's evolutionary', 'its binary', 'couldnt be me', and 'and thats an entirely different skillset than moving around rectangles'.

rules.rule: drop years and dated comparisons ('from 2017', 'made in 2014', '2019 squarespace template') and use a plain generic detail instead.
rules.evidence: 3 pairs (31, 33, 42). e.g. 'a 2019 squarespace template' became 'a squarespace template'; 'looked like it was made in 2014' became 'looks like the wrong template got used'.

rules.rule: don't write long posts where a quirky personal experiment is explained in step-by-step mechanism (kilos of blanket weight, a quoted axiom, a spelled-out inference chain) before a stretched 'visitors do the exact same thing' link to websites. both deleted drafts did this and then needed a reply with a dm pitch.
rules.evidence: 2 deleted drafts: the weighted-blanket / eleven-field contact form post and the lowercase follow-ups / 'axiom 7 contextual inference' post. published posts with the same reply format used shorter, simpler analogies.
